data.reason: The internet is down because gw.lan's WAN interface was never reconfigured after the ISP link bounced at ~02:01; the WAN watchdog's own logic already decided a reload was warranted at 02:30 and again at 02:40, but it runs in observe mode so it only logged "would_reload" and applied nothing, leaving vtnet0 holding the old lease (198.51.100.27) against a re-registered modem path.

data.cause: The internet is down because gw.lan's WAN interface was never reconfigured after the ISP link bounced at ~02:01; the WAN watchdog's own logic already decided a reload was warranted at 02:30 and again at 02:40, but it runs in observe mode so it only logged "would_reload" and applied nothing, leaving vtnet0 holding the old lease (198.51.100.27) against a re-registered modem path.
evidence: Timeline of outage from /var/log/system/latest.log: dpinger reports 'WAN_DHCP 198.51.100.1: sendto error: 64' at 02:01:58 and 'Alarm latency ... loss 100%' at 02:02:10 — WAN black hole starting right at the reported 02:01 onset.
Same log shows the alarm condition cleared at 02:28:31 ('sendto error: 64 cleared'), i.e. the next-hop path came back up ~13 min before now, yet connectivity is still absent.

ping -c 3 -n 198.51.100.1 -> 3 packets transmitted, 0 received, 100% packet loss; ping -c 3 -n 1.1.1.1 -> also 100% loss. ARP still has an entry for 198.51.100.1 (arp -a -n), so L2 to the ISP CPE exists but no traffic flows.
ifconfig vtnet0: UP,BROADCAST,RUNNING,SIMPLEX,MULTICAST,LOWER_UP, 'status: active', inet 198.51.100.27 — physical/WAN link is healthy, so this is not a local NIC/cable fault.
netstat -rn: default route present via 198.51.100.1 on vtnet0 — routing table is intact, ruling out a lost default route.

/var/db/dhclient.leases.vtnet0 shows lease acquired from dhcp-server-identifier 203.0.113.67 with fixed-address 198.51.100.27, renewal not due until 2026/3/5 — the firewall is still running the pre-outage lease and never renewed it after the modem re-registered.

/var/db/wan-watchdog/events.jsonl: decision at 02:30:00 action='reload' reason='modem_operational' down_seconds=1440, then events 'would_reload' at 02:30 and 02:40 with mode='observe'. state.json: reloads_in_outage=2, last_action='reload' — the watchdog wants to reload the WAN but observe mode prevents it.

/var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-events.jsonl explains the trigger: 'No Ranging Response received - T3 time-out' (02:01:44), 'TFTP failed - configuration file NOT FOUND' (02:14:10), then 'Cable Modem Reboot ... registration complete' (02:28:21).

/var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-metrics.jsonl: cm status NOT_SYNCHRONIZED at 02:06, back to OPERATIONAL by 02:29 and still OPERATIONAL at 02:40 (min_snr 37.9) — the modem itself has recovered, so the remaining fault is on the firewall's WAN side, not a dead modem.
data.recommendation: Reconfigure/renew gw.lan's WAN interface (vtnet0) so it re-runs DHCP against the re-registered ISP path and replaces the stale 198.51.100.27 lease — this is exactly the action the watchdog already decided on at 02:30/02:40 but could not take in observe mode. Verify with ping to 198.51.100.1 and an outbound test afterwards. Separately, ask the ISP about the upstream T3 timeout / missing config file that started the bounce at 02:01, and consider moving the watchdog out of observe mode so future recoveries apply automatically.
data.detail: WAN left on a stale lease/config after the cable modem dropped and re-registered; needs a WAN reconfigure/renew
